NEURA introduces Neuron AI with touch, sound and memory

The locally running model is set for an eleven-minute laundry-handling demonstration at GTC Berlin.

Humanoids Daily ↗15 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Perception beyond cameras

NEURA announced Neuron AI on October 14, with Humanoids Daily reporting the details the next day. Its Perception-Language-Action model combines 3D vision, force and touch, audio, robot state and language with memory, targeting tasks such as recognizing that a component has locked into place.

Training and local execution

The company identifies five embodiments: 4NE1 generations 3 and 4, a wheeled version and two further bimanual platforms. Training combines physical robot data, simulation and sensor-suit demonstrations. Inference runs on the robot without requiring the cloud, while Neuraverse is intended to support customer-specific skill adaptation.

An upcoming demonstration

At GTC Berlin on October 20–22, NEURA plans an eleven-minute sequence spanning laundry sorting, washer loading and transfer to a dryer. That duration covers handling rather than a full wash-and-dry cycle. The announcement provides no repeated-run success rate, intervention count or measured Time-to-Skill result.
